prompt:
Generate one high-quality cinematic 16:9 image for the specified section, not a generic slide or dashboard. No letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, arrows, diagrams, interface, checkmarks, traffic-light statuses or readable documents. The compositor adds every semantic mark independently. Do not invent a completed publication, a live security test, a solved outing, approval or consensus. Fictional editorial staging, not documentary evidence. Rich material detail, carefully controlled light, credible objects and hands. Keep designated annotation zones visually quiet. Never fill quiet zones with invented panels. Reference images establish cast and room identity only; follow this section's camera and blocking.
VISUAL FORMAT: forensic-counterexample
TEACHING PURPOSE: Make one changed identifier visibly defeat the authorization claim.
CAMERA: Top-down macro of a single specimen on an investigator's light table.
Forensic light table at night: a single unmarked translucent specimen slide lies diagonally in the LOWER LEFT, illuminated by a narrow amber inspection light. A magnifying lens rests at the far left edge, partly cropped. Vast clean black-to-deep-blue glass area across CENTER and RIGHT for exact before/after typography and a returned label. No text, no circuit, no evidence stamps. Elegant investigation mood, visibly different from a workstation or dashboard.
COMPOSITING INTENT: A large replaced identifier runs diagonally across the specimen area; the ALLOW result dominates the right, with an explicit no-grant/no-live-effect limitation beneath.
SEMANTIC AUTHORITY FOR CONTEXT ONLY, NEVER RENDER THESE WORDS: FROZEN RULE / LOCAL EVALUATION. Try an unrecognized name: publish alias. The expression still returns allow. Which checked fact establishes permission to publish? None. This counterexample breaks the claim that this name test establishes authorization. It does not demonstrate an escaped effect on a live platform.
